title: Mathematical Expression Syntax and Interpretation
scope: The compositional interpretation of mathematical expressions: variables, constants, set membership, operators and binding conventions determine what an expression denotes. The object is the method of parsing and translating expressions while preserving scope and meaning.

includes: Set-builder expressions and operator precedence
Free and bound index interpretation
excludes: Individual notation entries or a book-wide symbol glossary
Truth conditions for quantified propositions in math.logic_quantifiers

title: Functions and Composition
scope: Functions assign a unique output to each element of a specified domain. Composition, images, preimages and inverses explain how mappings transform sets and how mappings can be combined.

includes: Domain, codomain, injectivity and surjectivity

title: Algebraic Equations and Equivalent Transformations
scope: Solving elementary algebraic equations by transformations that preserve their solution sets, with explicit domain restrictions and checks for extraneous or lost solutions.

excludes: Linear systems and elimination in linalg.linear_systems_subspaces

title: Algebraic Inequalities
scope: Solving elementary inequalities by tracking order, sign and domain restrictions through algebraic transformations. Solution sets are represented as intervals or constrained subsets.

title: Power Functions and Roots
scope: Real power functions and roots as transformations of a variable base, including exponent laws and their domain restrictions. The scope connects algebraic manipulation to growth and inverse-root reasoning.

title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
scope: Exponential functions and their logarithmic inverses, interpreted through multiplicative growth and additive logarithmic coordinates. The inverse relationship unifies their domains, identities and elementary equation transformations.

includes: Change of logarithm base

title: Mathematical Logic and Quantifiers
scope: The truth-conditional structure of mathematical propositions built from connectives, predicates and quantifiers. Quantifier order, variable binding and negation determine what a statement asserts and what counts as a counterexample.

excludes: Knowledge-base representation and automated logical inference in AI-KR
A proof or theorem as an individual Formal Object

title: Mathematical Proof Methods
scope: Constructing and evaluating mathematical arguments by matching a proposition to direct proof, contrapositive reasoning, contradiction, cases or induction. The unifying question is how assumptions and logical form determine a valid proof strategy.

includes: Induction hypotheses and counterexamples to invalid arguments

title: Sequences and Indexed Families
scope: Sequences and more general indexed families as assignments from an index set to values. Finite sums, products, index ranges and reindexing express operations on these families.

excludes: Convergence and infinite-series tests in analysis.sequences_series

title: Complex Numbers and Polar Representation
scope: Complex numbers as an extension of real arithmetic with Cartesian and polar representations. Modulus, argument, conjugation and Euler representation connect arithmetic to rotations and scaling in the plane.

includes: Conversion between representations and elementary complex powers

title: Combinatorial Counting
scope: Determining the size of finite collections by decomposing choices, constructing bijections and correcting overcounting. Permutations, combinations and inclusion-exclusion are methods for expressing the same enumeration problem.

title: Recurrence Relations
scope: Sequences specified by earlier values and initial conditions, and methods for deriving or verifying their explicit behavior. Recursive definitions are interpreted as mathematical constraints rather than program execution.

includes: First-order and elementary linear recurrences
excludes: Program recursion and dynamic programming in cs.recursion_dp

title: Graph Structure
scope: Graphs as vertices connected by edges, with directedness, adjacency, paths, cycles and connectivity specifying their mathematical structure.

excludes: Graph traversal and optimization algorithms in cs.graph_algorithms

title: Trees and Rooted Tree Structure
scope: Connected acyclic graphs and their rooted variants, characterized through unique paths, parent-child relationships, leaves and subtrees. Recursive decomposition explains tree structure independently of any storage implementation.

title: Binary Relations and Equivalence Classes
scope: Binary relations and the reflexive, symmetric and transitive structure that makes a relation an equivalence relation. Equivalence classes and quotient sets connect pairwise relatedness to a partition of a set.

title: Partial Orders
scope: Reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive relations that organize elements by comparison. Chains, incomparable elements, bounds and order diagrams describe structure without assuming every pair is comparable.

title: Vectors and Affine Geometry
scope: Vectors as quantities combined by addition and scalar multiplication, interpreted geometrically as displacements. Linear and affine combinations describe lines, planes and geometric configurations.

excludes: Inner products, norms and orthogonal projection

title: Matrices as Linear Maps
scope: Matrices represent finite-dimensional linear transformations relative to coordinates. Matrix-vector multiplication, matrix composition, transpose and inversion are interpreted through the associated linear maps.

title: Linear Systems and Elimination
scope: Solution sets of simultaneous linear equations and their computation by row operations and elimination. Consistency, free variables and rank connect an equation system to its family of solutions.

title: Vector Spaces and Subspaces
scope: Vector spaces and subsets closed under linear combinations, including spans, null spaces and ranges. The scope identifies when a set is a linear space and how algebraic constraints define subspaces.

title: Bases and Coordinates
scope: Bases provide unique coordinate descriptions of vectors in a finite-dimensional space. Linear independence, dimension and changes of basis explain when and how representations can be converted.

title: Vector Norms
scope: Norms measure vector magnitude through positivity, homogeneity and the triangle inequality. Norm-induced distance and comparisons among standard finite-dimensional norms describe geometric size without assuming an inner product.

title: Inner Products and Orthogonal Projection
scope: Inner products supply angles and orthogonality, enabling decomposition into components parallel and perpendicular to a subspace. Orthogonal projection is understood as the closest-point construction within this geometry.

excludes: PCA as a statistical learning method

title: Eigenvalues and Spectral Decomposition
scope: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and invariant subspaces describe how a linear map acts along distinguished directions. Diagonalization and the spectral structure of symmetric or Hermitian maps provide representations through these directions.

excludes: PCA as a learned dimensionality-reduction method
Singular value decomposition of general rectangular maps

title: LU Factorization
scope: A matrix decomposition into lower and upper triangular factors, including permutation factors when needed. Its algebraic connection to elimination explains how the factors encode successive equation reductions.

excludes: Floating-point pivot-selection analysis and numerical performance

title: QR Factorization
scope: A matrix decomposition into orthonormal directions and an upper-triangular coordinate factor. The decomposition links orthogonalization to representations of column spaces and least-squares geometry.

title: Singular Value Decomposition
scope: A linear map decomposed into orthonormal input and output directions with nonnegative singular values. This representation explains rank, pseudoinverses and optimal low-rank matrix approximation.

title: Tensors and Multilinear Maps
scope: Tensors as multilinear objects and their representation by coordinate arrays. Tensor products, index transformations and contractions express operations that respect the underlying vector spaces.

excludes: Array memory layout, broadcasting APIs and accelerator runtimes

title: Limits of Functions
scope: Computing and interpreting finite, one-sided and infinite limits of real functions. Local behavior near a point is distinguished from the function value at that point.

excludes: Derivative computation as an instantaneous rate

title: Single-Variable Differentiation
scope: The derivative as local linear rate of change for a real-valued function of one real variable. Differentiation rules and tangent approximations make the operation calculable and interpretable.

includes: Single-variable product, quotient and chain rules
excludes: Analysis of hypotheses underlying differentiation theorems

title: Single-Variable Integration
scope: Definite integrals as accumulated signed quantity and antiderivatives as a method for evaluating them. Substitution and integration by parts connect the accumulation and differentiation viewpoints.

title: Partial Derivatives and Gradients
scope: First-order variation of a scalar field along coordinate and directional changes. Partial derivatives assemble into a gradient whose pairing with a direction gives the directional derivative when differentiability holds.

title: Multivariable Chain Rule
scope: Differentiating a composition of multivariable maps by composing their local derivative maps. Dependency paths and compatible input-output dimensions determine how intermediate variables contribute.

title: Jacobian Matrices
scope: The matrix representation of the first derivative of a vector-valued map. Its action gives a local linear approximation and its determinant, when square, describes local signed volume scaling.

title: Hessian Matrices
scope: The matrix of second partial derivatives of a scalar-valued function and its role in local quadratic curvature. Directional second derivatives and symmetry conditions connect entries to local shape.

title: Taylor Approximation
scope: Approximating a sufficiently differentiable function near a point by a polynomial determined by its derivatives. The remainder distinguishes a local approximation from an exact identity and determines its usable accuracy.

includes: Single-variable and multivariable local expansions
excludes: Global convergence of infinite power series

title: Divergence and Curl
scope: Differential operators that describe local source density and local circulation of a vector field. Their component formulas are interpreted through flux and rotation in Euclidean space.

excludes: Integral evaluation over curves and surfaces

title: Line and Surface Integrals
scope: Accumulating scalar or vector fields along parametrized curves and surfaces, including circulation and flux. Boundary-to-interior integral identities connect these global accumulations to local field derivatives.

includes: Use of Green, Stokes and divergence identities under stated conditions
excludes: Individual theorem statements as separate Formal Objects

title: Multiple Integration
scope: Integrating over regions in Euclidean spaces of dimension greater than one by describing their geometry and setting up iterated integrals. Bounds and order of integration express the same accumulated quantity.

title: Change of Variables in Integration
scope: Transforming an integral between coordinate systems by mapping the domain and accounting for local volume scaling with the absolute Jacobian determinant. Applicability conditions prevent overcounting or singular-coordinate errors.

excludes: Abstract changes between measures using a Radon-Nikodym density

title: Completeness of the Real Numbers
scope: The least-upper-bound structure of the real numbers and how it supports existence and convergence arguments. Bounds, suprema, infima and Cauchy behavior are connected within the ordered real field.

title: Convergence of Real Sequences
scope: Rigorous convergence and divergence of real sequences using quantified limits, subsequences and Cauchy or monotonicity arguments. The scope analyzes limiting behavior rather than indexed notation.

title: Infinite Series
scope: Infinite sums defined through partial-sum limits, including absolute and conditional convergence. Convergence tests, rearrangement restrictions and power-series intervals explain when and how an infinite sum is meaningful.

title: Continuity of Real Functions
scope: Continuity and uniform continuity of real functions through epsilon-delta and sequential characterizations. Local hypotheses, domain restrictions and interval or compact-domain consequences govern rigorous continuity arguments.

excludes: General topological continuity by open preimages

title: Rigorous Differentiation of Real Functions
scope: Differentiability of real functions as a limit property, and reasoning about when derivative-based conclusions are justified. Mean-value reasoning and counterexamples distinguish differentiability, continuity and derivative continuity.

excludes: A catalogue of symbolic derivative rules
A particular theorem or proof as the Concept identity

title: Riemann Integrability and the Fundamental Theorem
scope: Riemann integration through upper and lower sums, integrability criteria and the conditions connecting accumulated integrals to derivatives. The central object is the rigorous integration framework and its relation to differentiation.

title: Convergence of Function Sequences
scope: Pointwise and uniform convergence of sequences of functions, distinguished by the order of quantifiers and control over the domain. These modes determine when limiting functions preserve continuity or permit exchanging limits with analytic operations.

excludes: Almost-everywhere and integral-convergence methods in measure theory

title: Fourier Series
scope: Representing periodic functions by harmonic coefficients and partial sums. Orthogonality, approximation and convergence modes explain what reconstruction by a trigonometric series means.

title: Fourier Transforms
scope: Transforming functions between spatial or temporal variables and continuous frequency variables. Inversion, convolution and norm relationships characterize when frequency-domain representations can be used and recovered.

excludes: Windowed spectrogram construction and audio-model features

title: Normed Spaces and Banach Spaces
scope: Normed vector spaces and completeness under the norm-induced metric. Function-space examples and norm convergence explain how limits can remain within a space and what Banach completeness adds.

excludes: Hilbert projection and orthonormal expansion theory

title: Hilbert Spaces
scope: Complete inner-product spaces and the interaction of norm convergence with orthogonality. Orthogonal projection and orthonormal expansions describe geometric approximation in potentially infinite-dimensional spaces.

excludes: General Banach spaces without inner-product structure

title: Bounded Linear Operators
scope: Linear maps between normed spaces whose output norm is uniformly controlled by the input norm. Operator norms, continuity and operator convergence describe their analytic behavior.

excludes: Optimization operators or numerical iteration schemes

title: Dual Spaces and Linear Functionals
scope: Continuous linear functionals on normed spaces and the dual space they form. Dual pairing and representation of functionals explain how linear measurements describe vectors and function-space elements.

title: Metric Spaces
scope: A set equipped with a distance satisfying the metric axioms. Balls, metric convergence and continuity express closeness without relying on Euclidean coordinates.

excludes: Completeness and compactness criteria as additional structures

title: Topological Spaces and Open Sets
scope: Topologies specify open sets and thereby neighborhoods, closed sets, closure, interior and continuity by preimages. This structure describes qualitative proximity without requiring a metric.

excludes: Connectedness and compactness as separate properties

title: Compactness
scope: Compactness through finite subcovers, with sequential characterizations where applicable. Compactness controls global behavior from local information and supports existence arguments under appropriate continuity assumptions.

excludes: Equating compactness with completeness or boundedness in arbitrary spaces

title: Completeness of Metric Spaces
scope: Metric spaces in which every Cauchy sequence has a limit in the space. Completion and completeness-based convergence arguments distinguish internal convergence from convergence in a larger ambient space.

excludes: The ordered-field completeness of the real numbers as the primary object

title: Connectedness
scope: The impossibility of decomposing a space into disjoint nonempty open pieces. Connected components, path connectedness and continuous images distinguish global continuity of a space from local proximity.

title: Product Topology
scope: The topology on a Cartesian product induced by coordinate projections. Basic open sets and coordinatewise convergence explain how component spaces combine without imposing a uniform distance across coordinates.

title: Topologies on Function Spaces
scope: Topological structures on collections of functions, including pointwise and compact-open constructions. Neighborhoods of functions determine what it means for functions to be close independently of a chosen norm.

title: Smooth Manifolds and Tangent Spaces
scope: Spaces locally represented by compatible smooth coordinate charts, with tangent spaces and differentials providing coordinate-independent local linear descriptions.

excludes: A chosen Riemannian metric and curvature

title: Riemannian Geometry
scope: Smooth manifolds equipped with smoothly varying inner products on tangent spaces. Length, geodesics and curvature describe intrinsic geometry induced by the metric.

title: Measure Spaces
scope: A measurable space equipped with a countably additive nonnegative measure. Sigma-algebras delimit measurable sets, and null sets and restricted measures describe how size is assigned consistently.

title: Measurable Functions
scope: Maps whose preimages preserve measurability, together with simple functions and pointwise construction rules. This specifies which transformations are compatible with measurable structures before assigning probabilistic meaning.

excludes: Random variables and distributions as probabilistic objects

title: Lebesgue Integration
scope: Integration of measurable functions by approximation from simple functions, extended to integrable signed functions. Almost-everywhere equivalence and integrability determine the scope of the resulting accumulation operation.

excludes: Selecting hypotheses to exchange a limit and integral
Riemann integration as the primary construction

title: Limit and Integral Interchange
scope: Determining whether limits of measurable functions can pass through an integral by checking monotonicity, domination or lower-bound conditions. The object is the method of choosing and verifying sufficient hypotheses and recognizing failure cases.

includes: Application of monotone convergence, dominated convergence and Fatou-type bounds
excludes: Individual theorem statements or proofs as Concept records

title: Product Measures and Iterated Integration
scope: Constructing measures on product measurable spaces and relating product integrals to iterated integrals. Nonnegative or integrability hypotheses determine when changes in integration order are justified.

title: Densities Between Measures
scope: Absolute continuity and Radon-Nikodym densities express one measure relative to another. Integration against the new measure is translated into weighted integration against the reference measure under the required hypotheses.

excludes: Coordinate transformations and Jacobian factors as a calculus operation

title: Ordinary Differential Equation Initial-Value Problems
scope: Ordinary differential equations specify a trajectory through a time-local rate law, while initial conditions select a solution. Elementary solution methods and existence or uniqueness conditions define the mathematical initial-value problem.

title: Dynamical Systems and State Evolution
scope: A dynamical system evolves a state by a continuous-time flow or a discrete-time map. Trajectories, composition of evolution and invariant sets describe temporal behavior at the mathematical state-space level.

title: Equilibrium Stability
scope: Equilibria as states fixed by a dynamical evolution and stability as the response of nearby trajectories to perturbations. Local linearization and Lyapunov-style reasoning distinguish stability, attraction and instability under stated assumptions.

excludes: Choosing a feedback controller to achieve stability
A particular Lyapunov function or invariant as a standalone record

title: Linear Dynamical Systems
scope: Continuous and discrete state evolution governed by linear maps, including homogeneous and forced solutions. Matrix exponentials or powers and modal structure explain trajectories and their long-term behavior.

title: Partial Differential Equation Problems
scope: Partial differential equations constrain fields through derivatives in multiple independent variables. Differential order, linearity and initial or boundary conditions specify a problem, with heat, wave and potential equations illustrating distinct forms of spatial-temporal constraint.

excludes: An exhaustive catalogue of PDE solution methods

title: Probability Spaces and Events
scope: A probability space represents uncertain outcomes, measurable events, and their probabilities. The scope is constructing and interpreting event models and applying probability axioms to them.

title: Random Variables and Their Distributions
scope: A random variable maps outcomes to numerical values and induces a probability distribution. Distribution functions, mass functions, densities, and standard distribution families provide representations for computing probabilities of its values.

includes: Discrete and continuous laws and transformations of a single random variable
excludes: Characteristic and moment-generating transforms in probability.transforms

title: Joint Distributions and Marginalization
scope: A joint law describes several random variables together; marginalization obtains the law of a subset by summing or integrating out the remaining variables. The central object is this relationship between a multivariate law and its marginal views.

includes: Joint mass functions and densities
Marginalization of multivariate laws

title: Event Conditioning and Bayes’ Rule
scope: Event conditioning restricts a probability model to an event of positive probability and renormalizes it. Bayes’ rule and total probability express how event probabilities are recomputed and reversed under this operation.

title: Conditional Distributions
scope: A conditional distribution describes the law of one random variable when information about another is supplied. The scope includes constructing and using discrete and density-based conditional laws, with regular conditional laws as a rigorous extension.

excludes: Event-conditioning calculations as the primary object

title: Probabilistic Independence
scope: Independence states when joint probabilities factor into products of marginal probabilities. The scope includes independence of events and random variables, pairwise versus mutual independence, and the distinction between unconditional and conditional independence.

excludes: Graphical separation and inference algorithms in AI-PROBMODELS

title: Expectation and Moment Calculus
scope: Expectation averages a function of a random variable under its law. Linearity, integrability, raw moments, and conditional expectation provide the calculus for evaluating and decomposing such averages.

excludes: Variance and covariance as second-order dispersion and dependence measures

title: Variance and Covariance
scope: Variance and covariance describe second-order fluctuation through centered products. Their transformation rules and covariance matrices characterize dispersion of scalars and random vectors.

includes: Correlation as normalized covariance

title: Probability Distribution Transforms
scope: Characteristic, moment-generating, and probability-generating functions encode a distribution as an expectation of a transform kernel. Their common purpose is to recover distributional information and simplify sums of independent random variables while tracking existence conditions.

title: Modes of Convergence of Random Variables
scope: Almost-sure, in-probability, in-distribution, and mean-power convergence express different ways a sequence of random variables can approach a limit. Their implications and counterexamples determine which limiting operations a probabilistic argument can support.

excludes: Specific laws of large numbers and central-limit arguments

title: Laws of Large Numbers
scope: Laws of large numbers give conditions under which averages approach an expectation. The scope is selecting and applying weak or strong laws and checking their assumptions, rather than storing a single theorem statement.

title: Central Limit Methods
scope: Central limit methods approximate the distribution of suitably centered and scaled sums by a Gaussian limit under stated assumptions. The scope includes normalization, applicability checks, and translating the limit into probability approximations.

title: Concentration Inequalities
scope: Concentration methods bound the probability that a random quantity deviates from a reference value using moment, boundedness, or tail assumptions. The scope is deriving and choosing finite-sample bounds, including their dependence on sample size and deviation scale.

excludes: Model-class generalization bounds as the learning-theory object

title: Stochastic Process Specification
scope: A stochastic process is a family of random variables indexed by time or another parameter. Finite-dimensional distributions, sample paths, and filtrations specify respectively its joint laws, realizations, and available information.

excludes: Particular Markov, martingale, or Brownian process theories
Execution ledgers and persistent agent state

title: Markov Chains and Processes
scope: The Markov property specifies a process whose conditional future law depends on the present state rather than the full past. Transition kernels, transition composition, and state behavior give a reusable framework for analyzing discrete- and continuous-time Markov models.

title: Stationary Stochastic Processes
scope: Stationarity describes which process distributions or moments remain invariant under shifts of the index origin. Strict and weak stationarity, covariance functions, and counterexamples distinguish forms of temporal invariance.

includes: Strict and weak stationarity
Lag-dependent covariance structure
excludes: Time-series forecasting and fitted temporal models

title: Martingales
scope: A martingale has a conditional expectation of future value equal to its present value relative to a filtration. Conditional-expectation arguments, stopping, and convergence form the scope for analyzing fair-process behavior under explicit hypotheses.

title: Brownian Motion
scope: Brownian motion is a continuous-path stochastic process characterized by its Gaussian increment law and independent increments. The scope is reasoning from these properties about its finite-dimensional laws, scaling, and path variation.

excludes: Itô integration and SDE solution methods

title: Itô Stochastic Calculus
scope: Itô calculus defines integration against Brownian motion and a change-of-variables rule reflecting quadratic variation. It treats stochastic integrals and their algebraic and probabilistic properties.

title: Stochastic Differential Equations
scope: A stochastic differential equation specifies evolution through drift and stochastic forcing. The scope includes interpreting integral solutions, checking conditions for existence and uniqueness, and solving representative equations.

excludes: Construction of the Itô integral itself
Learned score models or diffusion training objectives

title: Sampling Distributions
scope: A sampling distribution is the distribution of a statistic under repeated samples from a specified population model. The scope is relating population, sample, statistic, and standard error for finite-sample inference.

excludes: Dataset collection, labeling, and mixture policies

title: Point Estimation and Estimator Risk
scope: Point estimation maps a sample to a parameter estimate, with bias, variance, and loss-based risk describing its performance. The scope is constructing and comparing estimators under a stated sampling model and target.

excludes: Predictive generalization error of learned models

title: Likelihood-Based Estimation
scope: Likelihood treats observed data as fixed and compares parameter values by the probability model they assign to those observations. Maximization, score equations, and information describe how this comparison produces and analyzes maximum-likelihood estimates.

excludes: Probability of data as a function of observations

title: Bayesian Parameter Inference
scope: Bayesian parameter inference updates a prior distribution over unknown parameters with a likelihood to obtain a posterior. Posterior summaries, MAP estimates, and posterior predictive distributions express inferences from that update.

excludes: Bayes’ rule for events as a probability identity
MCMC as a general computational method

title: Confidence Intervals and Confidence Sets
scope: Confidence-set procedures return parameter regions with specified repeated-sampling coverage under a model. The scope includes constructing sets and interpreting coverage, width, and the distinction from posterior credible probability.

excludes: Bayesian credible sets as posterior summaries

title: Statistical Hypothesis Testing
scope: Statistical tests use data to decide whether to reject a specified null hypothesis under controlled error criteria. Test statistics, rejection regions, p-values, power, and alternatives define the decision procedure.

title: Asymptotic Statistical Inference
scope: Asymptotic inference derives large-sample behavior of estimators and statistics from probability limits. Consistency, asymptotic normality, the delta method, and local approximations provide a common calculus for approximating inferential uncertainty.

excludes: Proof and general applicability of probability limit theorems

title: Statistical Resampling
scope: Statistical resampling approximates a sampling distribution by repeatedly recomputing a statistic on constructed versions of observed data. Bootstrap, jackknife, and permutation schemes are compared by what distribution each construction approximates and the assumptions making that approximation relevant.

excludes: Sampling from a known target distribution by Monte Carlo

title: Monte Carlo Estimation
scope: Monte Carlo estimation approximates expectations using simulated samples. Estimation error, importance weighting, and variance reduction describe the relation between the sampling distribution and the target integral.

excludes: Markov-chain construction for a stationary target
Action-value Monte Carlo learning in RL

title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo
scope: MCMC constructs a Markov chain with a desired invariant distribution to approximate expectations and draw dependent samples. Transition design, Metropolis–Hastings and Gibbs updates, and dependence-aware convergence diagnostics define the computational method.

excludes: Markov process theory without a target-sampling task
Bayesian inference as the prior-to-posterior reasoning object

title: Statistical Experimental Design
scope: Experimental design chooses assignments and measurement structure so that specified effects or parameters can be estimated under controlled sources of variation. Randomization, blocking, replication, and factorial contrasts are mechanisms for connecting a design to the estimand and its uncertainty.

excludes: AI benchmark construction and evaluation ablations as operational protocols

title: Shannon Information and Entropy
scope: Self-information assigns information content to an outcome through its probability, and Shannon entropy averages that content over a distribution. The scope is this event-to-average construction, its interpretation, and discrete versus differential-entropy distinctions.

title: Joint and Conditional Entropy
scope: Joint and conditional entropy account for uncertainty shared across or remaining within several random variables. The entropy chain rule connects total uncertainty to successive conditional contributions.

includes: Conditional differential entropy where defined

title: Cross-Entropy
scope: Cross-entropy measures expected negative log probability assigned by a reference distribution to outcomes from a target distribution. The scope covers its computation and interpretation as expected log-loss or mismatched coding cost, with support conditions explicit.

excludes: KL divergence as relative distribution discrepancy

title: Kullback–Leibler Divergence
scope: KL divergence compares two probability laws through an expected log density ratio. Its directionality, support requirements, and relationship to cross-entropy characterize what distributional discrepancy it measures.

title: Mutual Information
scope: Mutual information measures statistical dependence through the discrepancy between a joint law and the product of its marginals. Conditional mutual information and entropy reduction express the same dependence question when additional information is available.

excludes: Decision value of information measured by utility

title: Lossless Source Coding
scope: Lossless source coding represents source symbols or sequences with uniquely decodable codes. The scope connects decodability constraints and expected code length to source probabilities, including constructive prefix-coding methods.

title: Rate–Distortion Theory
scope: Rate–distortion theory characterizes the information rate required to represent a source within an expected distortion constraint. It specifies the source, reproduction variable, distortion measure, and optimization defining the rate–distortion trade-off.

excludes: Relevance-variable preservation as an information bottleneck

title: Information Bottleneck
scope: The information bottleneck formulates a compressed representation that limits information retained about an input while preserving information about a designated relevance variable. Its information constraints and objective define the representation-selection problem.

excludes: A claim that all neural training follows this principle
Reconstruction-distortion constraints without a relevance variable

title: Communication Channels and Capacity
scope: A communication channel is specified by a conditional output law given an input. Channel capacity asks for the maximum information rate supported by that channel under a stated input constraint and coding model.

includes: Discrete memoryless channel examples
Mutual-information optimization over input laws

title: Optimization Problem Formulation
scope: An optimization problem specifies decision variables, an objective, and a feasible set. Feasible directions, local versus global optima, and level-set geometry describe what a solution means before choosing an algorithm.

title: Convex Optimization Geometry
scope: Convex sets and convex functions give optimization problems a geometry in which local and global optimality can be related. The scope is recognizing convex structure, applying convexity-preserving operations, and reasoning with supporting hyperplanes and subgradients.

title: Gradient Descent
scope: Gradient descent iteratively moves opposite the gradient of a differentiable objective. Step-size choices, descent conditions, and stopping criteria define how the method approaches a stationary point under stated assumptions.

title: Momentum and Accelerated Gradient Methods
scope: Momentum methods augment a gradient update with information from previous iterates or velocities. Heavy-ball and accelerated-gradient recurrences are compared through their update state and assumption-dependent behavior.

title: Stochastic Gradient Optimization
scope: Stochastic gradient optimization updates an objective using sampled or noisy gradient estimates. Sampling variance, step schedules, and adaptive scaling explain how update rules manage uncertainty in gradient information.

excludes: Deterministic momentum acceleration as a separate update-state method
Neural training dynamics and hyperparameter recipes

title: Constrained Optimality and Lagrange Multipliers
scope: Constrained optimality uses feasible directions and multipliers to characterize candidate optima subject to equalities and inequalities. Constraint qualifications, complementary slackness, and KKT conditions specify when those characterizations apply.

excludes: Lagrangian dual bounds as an independent optimization problem

title: Lagrangian Duality
scope: Lagrangian duality forms an optimization problem over multipliers to obtain bounds on a primal problem. Weak and strong duality, the duality gap, and saddle-point structure describe the relation between the two problems.

title: Second-Order Optimization
scope: Second-order methods use local curvature models to choose optimization steps. Newton and quasi-Newton updates, damping, and trust regions connect the model to stable progress on smooth objectives.

excludes: Root finding without a minimization objective

title: Proximal Optimization
scope: Proximal methods update variables by solving a local distance-regularized subproblem, often separating smooth and nonsmooth objective terms. Proximal maps and proximal-gradient updates define the mechanism for composite objectives.

excludes: Curvature estimation as the defining update mechanism

title: Floating-Point Arithmetic and Rounding Error
scope: Floating-point arithmetic represents real-number approximations with finite precision and rounding. Representation range, rounding propagation, cancellation, overflow, and underflow explain discrepancies between exact arithmetic and computed results.

title: Conditioning and Numerical Stability
scope: Conditioning describes how problem outputs respond to input perturbations, while stability describes errors introduced by an algorithm. Forward and backward error analysis separates inherent sensitivity from computational behavior.

includes: Condition numbers and backward-error interpretation
excludes: Floating-point formats as the main object

title: Numerical Linear System Solvers
scope: Numerical linear-system solvers approximate solutions of matrix equations using factorizations or iterative residual correction. Pivoting, preconditioning, residuals, and conditioning govern algorithm selection and error interpretation.

title: Numerical Least Squares
scope: Numerical least-squares methods solve residual-minimization problems with attention to conditioning and rank. QR- and SVD-based computation distinguish stable solution procedures from algebraically equivalent but numerically sensitive formulations.

title: Numerical Eigenvalue and Singular-Value Computation
scope: Numerical spectral methods approximate eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and singular subspaces through iterative or factorization-based computation. Residuals, separation, and perturbation sensitivity determine the interpretation of computed spectral quantities.

excludes: Spectral theorem and exact factorization theory
PCA as a statistical learning method

title: Numerical Quadrature
scope: Numerical quadrature approximates definite integrals by weighted function evaluations. Rule construction, truncation error, and adaptive refinement relate a finite evaluation budget to integration accuracy.

title: Numerical Differentiation
scope: Numerical differentiation approximates derivatives from sampled function values. Finite-difference formulas and step-size selection balance truncation error against rounding and data noise.

title: Numerical Time Integration
scope: Numerical time integration approximates differential-equation trajectories by successive finite steps. Local and global error, consistency, stability, and stiffness explain the relationship between the discrete iteration and the target continuous dynamics.

excludes: Mathematical existence and exact differential-equation solutions
Generic fixed-point iteration for algebraic problems

title: Automatic Differentiation
scope: Automatic differentiation evaluates derivatives of a program by composing local derivative rules along its executed operations. Forward and reverse accumulation, Jacobian-vector products, and vector-Jacobian products define how derivatives are computed without finite-difference approximation.

title: Algorithmic Resource Analysis
scope: Analyzes time and space consumption as functions of input size, including asymptotic bounds and worst-case, average-case, and amortized accounting.

title: Computational Complexity Classes
scope: Classifies decision problems by resource-bounded computational models and uses reductions to compare tractability and hardness.

excludes: The calculational analysis of a particular implementation

title: Data Structure Design
scope: Relates an abstract collection and its supported operations to concrete representations and operation costs. The object is representation selection and invariant-preserving operations, with sequences, maps, heaps, and search trees as contrasting realizations.

includes: Representation invariants as objects of design reasoning, not individual invariant records

title: Recursive Algorithm Design
scope: Defines algorithms through smaller subproblem calls, base cases, and a termination argument, and relates recursive execution to its call structure.

excludes: Mathematical recurrence relations as formal objects

title: Dynamic Programming
scope: Constructs a state and recurrence for overlapping subproblems and evaluates them by memoization or tabulation, including solution reconstruction.

excludes: Bellman policy and value algorithms specific to sequential decision problems

title: Graph Traversal and Structural Analysis
scope: Explores an explicit graph through breadth-first or depth-first traversal to determine reachability, traversal trees, ordering, and connected structure.

title: Shortest-Path Algorithms
scope: Computes minimum-cost routes in weighted graphs by maintaining and relaxing distance estimates, with algorithm choice governed by weight and graph assumptions.

excludes: Heuristic search over implicitly generated AI states

title: Minimum Spanning Trees

includes: Information available at each decision and the choice of horizon or return criterion
excludes: Algorithms that learn policies or values

scope: Formulates fully observed sequential choice through states, actions, transition probabilities, rewards, and policies under the Markov assumption.

excludes: Learning transitions, values, or policies from interaction

includes: The role of Bayesian belief updating in the decision formulation
excludes: Persistent execution state and context assembly

scope: Models interdependent choices through players, strategies, information, and payoffs and analyzes best responses and equilibrium under specified game assumptions.

A causal graph instance as a Formal Object

Counterfactual inference about a particular observed unit

scope: Determines when and how conditioning or standardizing over covariates can remove confounding bias for a specified causal effect under explicit graphical assumptions.

Counterfactual inference for a specified individual

scope: Infers hypothetical outcomes under a changed mechanism for a unit or population constrained by factual evidence, using an explicit causal model and assumptions linking factual and hypothetical worlds.

excludes: Claims that observational association alone determines causality
Effect estimation on an already specified causal model

includes: Open-loop versus closed-loop structure and state-feedback realization

excludes: A particular Lyapunov proof as a Formal Object

title: Control-System Controllability
scope: Determines which states can be reached by admissible inputs and analyzes controllable subspaces and input placement under a stated state-space model.

title: Control-System Observability
scope: Determines whether internal states can be distinguished from output histories and analyzes observable subspaces and sensor placement under a stated state-space model.

title: Optimal Control
scope: Chooses a control trajectory or feedback law to optimize a cost subject to dynamical evolution and control constraints, relating the objective to state and control trajectories.

title: Model Predictive Control
scope: Controls a system by repeatedly solving a finite-horizon model-based optimization, executing an initial control action, and updating the problem from new state information.

excludes: Unconstrained claims of stability without stated conditions

title: Robust Control
scope: Designs and analyzes controllers against a specified set of plant uncertainties or disturbances, making the protected behavior and uncertainty bounds explicit.

excludes: Probabilistic noise models as the sole uncertainty description

title: Stochastic Control
scope: Designs control policies for dynamical systems with probabilistic disturbances or observations under expected-cost or probabilistic performance criteria.

title: System Identification
scope: Infers a dynamical input-output or state-space model from controlled-system observations, linking excitation, model structure, estimation, and validation to intended control use.

excludes: Causal discovery of a structural graph

title: Statistical Learning Problem Formulation
scope: Formulate learning through an observation distribution, hypothesis class, loss, population risk and empirical risk. Distinguish fitting on observed data from the target of prediction on unseen data.

title: Linear Regression
scope: Model a scalar response as a linear function of features and fit it through squared-error risk, including regularized estimation and interpretation of fitted coefficients.

title: Linear Classification
scope: Construct linear decision functions for labeled prediction and fit them using classification losses, including perceptron and binary logistic models.

title: Probabilistic Predictive Modeling
scope: Formulate supervised prediction through conditional or joint probabilistic models and use fitted distributions to produce predictions. Contrast generative and discriminative prediction through a simple generative classifier such as Naive Bayes.

includes: Predictive factorization assumptions and their consequences
excludes: Gaussian-process learning and mixture estimation as independent methods

title: Multiclass Prediction with Logits and Softmax
scope: Represent mutually exclusive class probabilities by logits normalized with softmax, and relate that parameterization to categorical prediction and cross-entropy training.

title: Decision Trees
scope: Learn a predictor by recursively partitioning feature space, selecting splits and controlling tree complexity through stopping or pruning.

excludes: Aggregation or sequential correction of multiple predictors in the ensemble-learning successor

title: Ensemble Learning
scope: Combine multiple predictors through aggregation or sequential correction, with bagging and boosting as contrasting construction mechanisms. Analyze how base-learner dependence and weighting affect the combined predictor.

title: Kernel Methods
scope: Construct learning methods using positive-semidefinite similarity functions and Gram matrices in place of explicit feature maps, including kernelized prediction.

title: Maximum-Margin Learning
scope: Fit decision boundaries by maximizing geometric margin, including soft-margin constraints, support vectors and hinge-loss formulations.

excludes: Kernel construction as an independent method

title: Gaussian Processes for Learning
scope: Use a Gaussian-process prior over functions to infer predictive distributions from data, emphasizing covariance specification and Gaussian-noise regression.

excludes: Bayesian optimization as a full decision algorithm

title: Instance-Based Learning
scope: Predict from stored examples using neighborhoods or distance-weighted local aggregation, with nearest-neighbor classification and regression as the central mechanisms.

excludes: All nonparametric statistical methods as an umbrella

title: Clustering
scope: Group observations through an explicit similarity or partition criterion, and reason about assignments and cluster structure using methods such as centroid and hierarchical clustering.

excludes: Probabilistic mixture likelihood and latent responsibilities

title: Mixture Models and Expectation-Maximization
scope: Represent an observation distribution as a weighted mixture with latent component assignments, and fit the model through responsibility estimation and parameter updates.

includes: Expectation-maximization for mixture estimation

title: Principal Component Analysis
scope: Estimate a low-dimensional linear representation by maximizing retained variance or minimizing orthogonal reconstruction error, including centering and component selection.

scope: Estimate linear latent components using independence assumptions to separate mixed signals, including ambiguity and identifiability of the recovered components.

scope: Construct low-dimensional embeddings that preserve selected neighborhood or intrinsic-geometric relationships among observations, and interpret distortions induced by that choice.

excludes: Data leakage detection and provenance tracking

excludes: Self-supervised representation learning without the labeled/unlabeled integration

excludes: Continual retention of prior task competence

title: Continual Learning
scope: Learn across successive tasks or changing data while managing retention of earlier competence, using replay, parameter constraints or architectural allocation as alternative mechanisms.

title: Dataset Lifecycle Management

excludes: Sampling examples from an existing training dataset

excludes: Specific defective records as Failure Mode instances

scope: Trace unintended information paths from targets, held-out observations or evaluation material into model fitting and selection, and design separation or detection procedures.

title: Preference and Feedback Data

title: Trajectory and Interaction Data
scope: Construct learning datasets from temporally linked observations, actions and feedback, preserving episode boundaries, collection-policy information and temporal alignment.

title: Feedforward Neural Networks

excludes: Perceptron learning as a linear classification algorithm

scope: Normalize neural activations using explicitly chosen axes and statistics, including learned affine parameters and differences between training and inference behavior.

title: Residual Connections
scope: Compose a learned transformation with a skip path so that a block modifies an existing representation, and analyze the resulting forward and gradient paths.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks
scope: Build neural networks from spatially or temporally shared local filters, relating stride, padding and pooling to receptive fields and transformation behavior.

title: Graph Neural Networks
scope: Compute learned node, edge or graph representations through neighborhood message passing and aggregation, with graph structure and permutation behavior made explicit.

title: Knowledge Distillation
scope: Train a student model to reproduce selected teacher outputs or internal representations, specifying the transfer targets, losses and teacher-student relationship.

excludes: Preference-based alignment as a separate training objective

excludes: Variational autoencoders and latent generative likelihoods

includes: Interpreting distribution-level diagnostics and their blind spots

Deep RL target/replay mechanisms

excludes: General embedding distance and geometry in representation.embeddings_geometry

excludes: LLM neural next-token training objective in llm.autoregressive_objective

excludes: A catalog of unrelated NLP sequence tasks

title: Sampled audio representation
