excludes: Spectrogram and learned feature extraction in audio.features_spectrogram

title: Time–frequency audio features
scope: Transforming sampled audio into localized time–frequency features for learning, including windowed spectra, spectrograms, and perceptually motivated frequency aggregation. The scope centers on the temporal/spectral resolution trade-off of feature construction.

excludes: Fourier/Harmonic analysis as a mathematical theory

title: Automatic speech recognition
scope: Inferring a word or token transcript from acoustic observations. The scope unifies acoustic-to-symbol modeling, uncertain alignment, and transcript decoding under the speech recognition objective.

title: Text-to-speech synthesis
scope: Generating a spoken waveform conditioned on text through linguistic/acoustic alignment, duration and prosody, and acoustic-to-waveform generation. The object is the coordinated text-to-speech synthesis system and its interfaces.

title: Query–key–value attention
scope: Computing a query-dependent aggregation of value vectors using compatibility between queries and keys. The object defines the roles and data flow of retrieval-like differentiable attention independent of a particular compatibility formula.

title: Scaled dot-product attention
scope: Computing attention weights from scaled query–key inner products and normalizing them before aggregating values. The scope covers tensor dimensions, scale, normalization, and the resulting operator.

excludes: General attention motivation and alternative compatibility functions

title: Attention masking and causal visibility
scope: Constraining which key positions each query can attend to by applying a visibility mask in the attention operator. Causal and padding masks are analyzed through information access and leakage.

title: Self-attention
scope: Applying query, key, and value projections to the same representation set to compute contextual interactions among its elements. The scope concerns within-sequence or within-set contextualization.

title: Cross-attention
scope: Using queries from one representation set to select and aggregate keys/values from another. The scope concerns the conditioning interface between the two sets and their potentially different lengths.

title: Multi-head attention
scope: Projecting representations into multiple attention heads and recombining their outputs. The scope covers head dimensions, independent attention computations, and the output projection as one operator.

excludes: Serving parallelism as a systems policy

title: Positional representations for attention
scope: Introducing order or relative position into attention-based sequence computation. Additive absolute encodings, relative biases, and rotary transformations are compared through how they modify representations or pairwise scores.

title: Transformer block
scope: Composing attention, feed-forward transformation, normalization, and residual updates into a Transformer representation block. The scope centers on information flow through the residual stream and the ordering of sublayers.

title: Transformer encoder and decoder architectures
scope: Arranging Transformer blocks and attention visibility into encoder-only, decoder-only, or encoder–decoder systems. The central question is how input/output conditioning requirements determine the arrangement.

includes: Bidirectional encoding
Causal decoding
Encoder–decoder cross-attention interface
excludes: A duplicate dense LLM architecture survey

title: Efficient attention mechanisms
scope: Changing the attention interaction pattern or algebra to constrain the cost of sequence mixing. The scope compares sparse connectivity and compressed or factorized interactions by the information paths and approximation they retain.

excludes: Exact attention kernel implementation without changing the interaction mechanism

title: Transformer key–value cache mechanism
scope: Reusing previously computed attention keys and values during autoregressive decoding. The scope explains cache content, position-dependent updates, and why past states can be reused under the decoding visibility structure.

excludes: Serving cache allocation, paging, eviction, and batching in aisystems.kv_memory
Persistent agent memory or execution state

title: Foundation-model pretraining and reuse
scope: Training a broadly reusable model before adapting or conditioning it for multiple downstream tasks. The scope concerns the shared-model lifecycle and the distinction between general pretraining and task-specific learning.

excludes: Specific language pretraining pipeline in llm.pretraining
Claims that all downstream tasks benefit from pretraining

title: Scaling and downstream transfer analysis
scope: Analyzing how changes in pretraining scale relate to downstream transfer under an explicit adaptation and evaluation setting. The object is a comparison framework separating pretraining fit, resource scale, and downstream task performance.

includes: Comparing scale changes at specified adaptation conditions
Distinguishing pretraining loss from downstream transfer performance
excludes: Specific LLM scaling-law fitting in llm.scaling
Unqualified empirical claims of emergent abilities

title: Foundation-model parameter adaptation
scope: Adapt a pretrained model through an explicitly chosen trainable parameter subset or update parameterization. Compare full updates, frozen components, inserted adaptation parameters and constrained update subspaces by their parameter interface and resource constraints, while taking the downstream transfer target as given.

excludes: Task-specific instruction/preference training signals in POSTTRAIN
Source-target transfer formulation and selection of transferable knowledge in representation.transfer_multitask

title: Autoregressive language-model training objective
scope: Training a neural language model to predict the next token from a prefix by minimizing token-sequence negative log likelihood. The scope connects language targets, shifted inputs, conditional factorization, and the token-level training loss.

title: Language-model pretraining design
scope: Designing the training stage that learns a language model from a text corpus, coupling corpus mixture, sequence construction, and training objective under a resource budget. The object is the pretraining pipeline interface, not the independent mathematics of each component.

title: Mixture-of-experts routing in language models
scope: Selecting and combining expert transformations for language-model token representations. The scope centers on router decisions, sparse activation, capacity, and load-balancing constraints within the model computation.

title: Language-model scaling analysis
scope: Modeling the relationship among language-model size, training data, computation, and predictive loss for resource-allocation analysis. The scope treats fitted scaling relationships as conditional models whose assumptions and extrapolation limits must be inspected.

excludes: Claims of universal fixed scaling exponents

title: Language-model decoding
scope: Converting next-token distributions into output sequences under a chosen generation objective. Sampling transformations and search-based choices are compared by how they change probability mass, sequence scores, and stopping behavior.

includes: Temperature, top-k, and top-p sampling
Greedy and beam-based sequence selection

title: In-context learning
scope: Conditioning a fixed-parameter language model on examples or task information so its predictions adapt within the current input. The scope distinguishes this input-conditioned behavior from parameter training and from simply assembling an input.

excludes: A claim that model parameters change during ordinary prompting

title: Instruction supervised fine-tuning
scope: Adapting a pretrained model by supervised learning on instruction-response examples, with the response target and loss exposure defined explicitly. The scope concerns learning instruction-following behavior through this training signal.

excludes: Pure prompt construction without parameter training

title: Preference-based reward modeling
scope: Learning a response-scoring function from relative preference feedback for use as a post-training optimization signal. The scope includes how comparison labels induce a scoring objective and what the learned score represents.

excludes: Direct policy optimization without a separately learned reward model

title: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
scope: Optimizing a pretrained model policy using a reward signal learned from human feedback, with reference-policy constraints and rollout-based training. The object is the feedback-to-reward-to-policy integration, independent of the particular optimizer.

includes: Human feedback, learned reward, policy rollouts, and reference constraint interfaces

title: Proximal policy optimization
scope: Updating a policy through a proximity-controlled surrogate objective using sampled policy ratios and advantage estimates. The scope includes clipped or penalized policy updates and their relationship to the data-collecting policy.

title: Direct preference optimization
scope: Optimizing a model policy directly from preferred and dispreferred response pairs through a reference-relative preference objective. The scope centers on the conversion from comparison evidence to policy updates without a separate rollout reward-model training loop.

excludes: Reward-model fitting as a separate learned scorer
Generic pairwise ranking without a policy-update target
Claims of universal superiority over RLHF

title: Rule-guided post-training
scope: Using explicit behavioral rules to generate critiques, revisions, or preference/target signals for model post-training. The central object is translating a normative rule specification into a trainable signal.

excludes: An individual rule or invariant as the Concept

title: Tool-use policy training
scope: Training a model to choose tool calls and arguments and to condition later decisions on tool feedback. Supervised interaction traces and reward-based interaction learning are alternative signals within this action/observation training interface.

excludes: General RL algorithms or API documentation

title: Chain-of-thought reasoning traces
scope: Using intermediate generated steps as part of a model output trajectory that precedes or supports a final answer. The scope distinguishes trace construction and use from the stronger claim that a displayed trace faithfully exposes internal computation.

excludes: Empirical claims that all traces are faithful

title: Self-consistency for model reasoning
scope: Sampling multiple reasoning trajectories and aggregating their final answers after defining answer equivalence. The object concerns the sampling-to-aggregation method and its dependence on agreement and sample diversity.

excludes: Generic statistical consistency of an estimator

title: Process supervision for model reasoning
scope: Training reasoning behavior with supervision attached to intermediate steps or transitions. The scope concerns step target construction, attribution, and the relation between local feedback and full-solution behavior.

title: Outcome supervision for model reasoning
scope: Training reasoning behavior using labels or rewards attached to completed solutions rather than each intermediate step. The scope concerns terminal target construction and what such feedback leaves unspecified about the reasoning path.

title: Reasoning verifiers
scope: Constructing or applying a check or scorer to a candidate reasoning step or solution for acceptance, ranking, or search guidance. The scope concerns the verifier interface and the distinction between checked validity and model-generated plausibility.

excludes: A single checked claim as a Concept

title: Reinforcement learning for model reasoning
scope: Training a model over reasoning trajectories with rewards tied to solution outcomes or checked steps. The scope integrates reasoning action granularity, reward availability, and policy updates, including the distinction between verifiable rewards and learned scoring signals.

excludes: Training all language behaviors from human preferences

title: Test-time search for model reasoning
scope: Allocating inference computation to generate, score, extend, and select reasoning trajectories before producing a final answer. The object centers on coupling a model generator, search controller, and optional verifier under a computation budget.

includes: Search over complete or partial reasoning candidates
Verifier-guided candidate selection
excludes: Agent orchestration of external tool actions

title: Digital Image Representation
scope: Represent an image as a sampled spatial signal with intensity or color channels, and relate pixel coordinates, resolution and local image structure to visual information. The object is the representation of visual input used before a particular recognition model.

title: Object Detection
scope: Infer a variable set of object locations and classes from an image, including localization targets, assignment of predictions to objects and resolution of overlapping detections.

title: Image Segmentation
scope: Assign image regions or pixels to semantic classes or object instances, connecting dense output structure with supervision and region consistency. Semantic and instance variants are compared through this common partitioning problem.

excludes: A catalog of all visual recognition tasks

title: Vision Transformers
scope: Encode images as patch or region tokens and use Transformer processing to build spatial visual representations. The scope is the adaptation of tokenization, spatial structure and readout to images.

excludes: Generic attention and Transformer block mechanics in TRANSFORMER

title: Three-Dimensional Visual Reconstruction
scope: Recover three-dimensional scene structure from visual observations by relating camera projection, depth and geometric consistency across views. The unifying inverse problem is what spatial structure is supported by the images.

title: Cross-Modal Representation Alignment
scope: Relate representations of corresponding content across modalities so that semantic correspondence is preserved despite different observation spaces. Scope covers alignment targets and correspondence constraints, rather than every method for combining modalities.

title: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning
scope: Learn cross-modal compatibility from matched and mismatched observations, specifying positive correspondence, negative construction and directional matching losses. The distinctive problem is learning a shared comparison from paired modalities.

excludes: Generic metric and contrastive objectives in representation.metric_contrastive

title: Multimodal Information Fusion
scope: Combine information from multiple modalities into a joint inference representation, choosing where and how cross-modal interaction occurs. Analyze complementary, conflicting or missing inputs through that combination mechanism.

title: Vision–Language Model Integration
scope: Connect a visual encoder to language processing so that linguistic outputs or queries can condition on visual content. Scope centers on the representation interface and cross-modal conditioning path in a vision–language system.

title: Multimodal Instruction Tuning
scope: Adapt a multimodal model to follow instructions referring to non-text evidence by aligning referenced regions, times or modality elements with response supervision. Diagnose mismatched, missing or conflicting evidence and instruction-response alignments within the training example.

excludes: Generic supervised instruction tuning in posttrain.sft_instruction

title: Cross-Modal Conditional Generation
scope: Generate content in one modality conditioned on information in another, specifying conditioning correspondence and the output representation. Scope is the cross-modal generation interface and consistency problem.

excludes: Generic generative model families in GEN
Following instructions as a training objective

title: Embodied Perception–Action Loop
scope: Couple sensing and physical action in a feedback loop in which actions change both the environment and subsequent observations. Scope addresses embodiment constraints on timing, sensing and action interpretation.

excludes: Generic agent control-loop architecture in agent.boundary_loop
Formal POMDP state and belief definitions

title: Robot Policy Learning
scope: Formulate learning a robot policy from physical observations and action data under embodiment constraints such as actuator limits, sensing delays and interaction cost. Scope is the integration of policy learning with a robot interface and data-collection loop.

excludes: A survey chapter of all robot learning

title: Robot Kinematics
scope: Relate robot joint configurations and velocities to body or end-effector poses and velocities through rigid transformations and kinematic mappings.

excludes: Forces, inertia and motion equations in robot dynamics

title: Robot Dynamics
scope: Relate robot motion, inertia, applied forces and torques through mechanical equations of motion, including forward and inverse dynamics.

excludes: Pose computation without forces in robot kinematics
Generic optimal control and system identification

title: Robot Navigation
scope: Integrate localization, spatial mapping and motion decisions to move an embodied system toward a destination under collision and sensing constraints. The knowledge object is how these components exchange spatial information during navigation.

title: Robotic Manipulation
scope: Select and execute physical interactions that change an object configuration, relating grasp or contact choices to feasible motion and task success. Scope centers on contact-mediated control of objects.

title: Vision–Language–Action Models
scope: Map visual observations and language instructions to embodied action outputs through a joint model interface. Scope covers action representation, temporal alignment and the grounding of instructions in executable behavior.

title: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer
scope: Transfer a learned embodied policy from simulation to physical execution by identifying and addressing mismatch in dynamics, sensing and action interfaces. Scope is the transfer procedure and its assumptions.

excludes: Claims that any transfer method guarantees physical success

title: Learned Environment Dynamics Models
scope: Learn a predictive environment transition model from interaction data, specifying inputs, predicted state or observations, and how one-step predictions compose into rollouts. The object is the learned transition model rather than the policy using it.

excludes: Policy learning using a model in rl.model_based

title: Latent World Models
scope: Represent an environment through learned latent states whose transitions support prediction of future observations or task-relevant quantities. Scope couples representation learning to rollout consistency and predictive sufficiency.

title: Planning with Learned World Models
scope: Use learned environment rollouts to compare prospective action sequences and choose actions, relating model uncertainty and rollout horizon to the planning interface. Scope is the integration between a learned predictor and a planner or controller.

excludes: Model predictive control derivations in control.mpc
The full learning algorithm loop of rl.model_based

title: Video-Based World Simulation
scope: Model future visual observations as environment evolution, specifying temporal continuity and any action or intervention conditioning required for simulation. Scope is the use of video prediction as a world simulator and the distinction between visual plausibility and transition fidelity.

excludes: Generic video generation without environment-simulation semantics
A claim that realistic video proves a valid causal simulator

title: Sparse Lexical Retrieval
scope: Retrieve documents by sparse term-based query and document representations, relating term weighting and matching to lexical relevance scores.

title: Retrieval Indexing
scope: Organize document or vector representations into an index supporting candidate retrieval and updates, relating access structure choices to query cost and approximation.

title: Retrieval Relevance Ranking
scope: Construct a query-dependent document ordering from relevance scores and combine scoring signals into a ranking function. Scope includes how relevance supervision defines pointwise, pairwise or listwise learning targets when the ranking function is learned.

title: Dense Retrieval
scope: Encode queries and candidate items into dense representations and retrieve by a learned similarity, linking encoder training to candidate search.

title: Retrieval Reranking
scope: Refine a retrieved candidate set using an additional relevance model, reasoning about candidate recall, joint query-document scoring and the two-stage cost boundary.

title: Retrieval Relevance Evaluation
scope: Assess a ranked retrieval result against query-specific relevance judgments, including graded relevance, rank sensitivity and incomplete judgment coverage. Scope is the connection between a retrieval task and the meaning of its ranking measures.

excludes: Generic benchmark design, confidence intervals and ablation in EVAL
Generation faithfulness and end-to-end RAG attribution

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Architecture
scope: Integrate a retriever and generator so that external retrieved evidence conditions a generated response. Scope is the end-to-end information flow and component contracts, including how evidence preparation, retrieval and generation fit together.

excludes: The evidence serialization details in rag.retrieval_generation_interface

title: Retrieval–Generation Evidence Interface
scope: Transform retrieved units into evidence that a generator can use, preserving source identity and relating chunk boundaries, metadata and evidence layout to answer needs.

excludes: General budgeted context selection in context.selection_assembly
Checking support of output claims in rag.grounding_attribution

title: Evidence Grounding and Attribution
scope: Relate generated statements to supporting retrieved evidence and expose the source of that support. Grounding and attribution are unified by the statement-to-evidence support relation, including unsupported or conflicting evidence.

excludes: An individual factual claim or source record
Determining whether supporting source assertions are themselves true about the world

title: Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation
scope: Use intermediate generated reasoning or evidence gaps to choose additional retrieval steps, updating the evidence available before producing an answer. Scope is the feedback loop between retrieval and generation and its stopping condition.

excludes: Generic agent planning and tool invocation

title: RAG Error Attribution
scope: Diagnose an end-to-end RAG error by separating evidence availability, retrieval selection, evidence presentation and generation support. Use component observations or controlled substitutions to locate the failed contract.

excludes: An inventory of named failure instances

title: Prompt and Instruction Design
scope: Express a task, constraints and expected response as instructions within a model invocation, keeping instruction roles and authority distinguishable from supporting data.

title: Context Budget and Position
scope: Analyze how a finite invocation window constrains the amount and placement of information presented to a model. Scope links capacity, ordering and accessibility as constraints on context design without asserting a universal positional-effect law.

excludes: Claiming an empirical effect size for positional sensitivity

title: Context Selection and Assembly
scope: Choose and arrange information for a particular invocation from available instructions, evidence, memories and execution records under a context budget. Selection and assembly form one exposure policy determining what the model can use now.

title: Progressive Context Disclosure
scope: Expose information incrementally when an invocation or trajectory step needs it, using compact references or summaries to decide when to load deeper detail.

title: Context Compression and Compaction
scope: Replace an overlong context with a shorter representation that preserves information required for continued work. Scope unifies selective compression and trajectory compaction through task-relevant information retention and loss analysis.

excludes: Authoritative state persistence or checkpoint recovery

title: Context Failure Diagnosis
scope: Diagnose whether an invocation error arises from missing, conflicting, irrelevant, stale or inaccessible exposed information, using the intended task and information sources as the reference. Scope is a reusable diagnosis method rather than a collection of failure instances.

title: Functional Classification of AI Memory
scope: Distinguish memory mechanisms by where information is retained, what content it represents and how it becomes available for later use. Treat parametric/external storage and episodic/semantic/procedural content as different classification dimensions.

excludes: A claim that a single biological taxonomy exhaustively describes model memory

title: Episodic Agent Memory
scope: Retain and retrieve situated past interactions or events with their temporal and contextual provenance so that later behavior can refer to specific experiences.

title: Semantic Agent Memory
scope: Retain reusable facts and abstractions detached from a single episode while preserving enough provenance to update or qualify them. Scope is the organization and use of this declarative memory content.

title: Procedural Agent Memory
scope: Retain reusable procedures or skills for later action and recover them in a form that can guide execution. Scope is the persistence, selection and adaptation of action knowledge, rather than facts about prior events.

title: Memory Retrieval
scope: Recover retained knowledge using task cues while accounting for memory content type, temporal relevance and provenance. Scope is the access policy over a memory store.

excludes: Generic retrieval ranking algorithms in IR
Choosing final invocation exposure in CONTEXT

title: Memory Consolidation
scope: Integrate new experiences or retrieved knowledge into retained memory by abstraction, deduplication or revision, preserving provenance and deciding what remains useful over time.

excludes: A biological account of human memory consolidation

title: AI Memory Architectures
scope: Coordinate memory storage, writing and retrieval mechanisms with an agent or model so that retained information can influence later behavior. Scope is the interface architecture and read/write lifecycle across memory components.

title: Execution State, Observation and Context Roles
scope: Distinguish environmental observations, recorded execution state and currently exposed model context by their roles and authority during ongoing execution. Explain how an observation becomes a record and how a record becomes context without making these roles identical.

excludes: Formal POMDP state, observation and belief relationships

title: Persistent Canonical Execution State
scope: Maintain a durable authoritative record of task progress, decisions and pending obligations across invocations. Scope distinguishes persistence from authority and specifies how execution consults and updates the canonical record.

excludes: An individual state file or invariant

title: Execution Task Ledgers
scope: Represent task obligations, progress and recorded outcomes in a durable ledger so that remaining work can be determined from explicit evidence.

title: Execution Checkpointing
scope: Capture a consistent resumable execution snapshot with sufficient references to reconstruct ongoing work at a defined boundary.

title: Execution Handoff and Reconstruction
scope: Transfer ongoing work by packaging durable state and evidence so another invocation or actor can reconstruct goals, completed work and pending actions. Handoff is assessed through the recipient reconstruction contract.

title: Execution State Reconciliation
scope: Compare recorded progress with current external observations, detect stale or conflicting records and reconcile the authoritative execution state before further action. Freshness is a condition checked within this reconciliation method.

title: Idempotent Execution Recovery
scope: Resume interrupted work without unintentionally duplicating completed effects by reconciling action identity, durable outcomes and retry decisions. Idempotency is used as part of the recovery protocol rather than treated as a guarantee of exactly-once execution.

title: Agent Control Loop and System Boundary
scope: An agent is analyzed as a system that selects actions from observations under a task objective and closes the loop through an environment. The object is the allocation of sensing, decision, action and termination responsibilities, independent of whether the decision component is an LLM.

excludes: Detailed observation/action interface design in agent.observation_action

title: Tool Invocation Contracts
scope: The contract connecting an agent-selected tool call to typed arguments, returned observations, declared effects and error outcomes. It covers interpreting and validating a call as an action rather than treating a tool schema as a guarantee that the action succeeded.

title: Agent Observation and Action Interfaces
scope: The representation and correspondence of observations and executable actions at an agent-environment boundary. It explains how observation limits, action granularity and returned feedback constrain the decisions an agent can express and check.

title: Interleaved Reasoning and Acting
scope: The ReAct-style orchestration pattern alternates explicit reasoning steps, tool actions and external observations within a task trajectory. Its scope is how observations update subsequent action selection, including distinctions between a generated rationale and externally established evidence.

excludes: A claim that generated rationales faithfully expose internal reasoning

title: Agent Task Decomposition and Plan Execution
scope: A task-level orchestration pattern turns a goal into dependent subgoals, assigns executable steps and uses their completion conditions to advance the agent. Decomposition is considered together with execution because the object is the interface from an agent plan to actual work.

excludes: Classical and hierarchical planning theory in AI-PLANNING
Runtime budget and cancellation enforcement in harness.task_control
Revision of an existing plan after feedback

title: Feedback-Driven Agent Replanning
scope: An orchestration method compares observed task progress with an existing plan, identifies invalid steps and revises the remaining work. It owns the agent-level triggering and use of replanning rather than planning theory.

title: Agent Reflection and Self-Correction
scope: A pattern uses critique of an agent attempt, possibly with external feedback, to generate corrective guidance for a subsequent attempt. It distinguishes proposed self-criticism from verified error evidence and does not imply guaranteed improvement.

excludes: Memory storage and consolidation of lessons

title: Computer-Use Agent Interaction
scope: An agent grounds task actions in a graphical computer interface, executes input events and checks the resulting screen or accessibility observations. The unifying challenge is closing a task loop through an interface whose visible controls and state may change.

excludes: Implementation of the execution sandbox or ACI

title: Browser Agent Navigation and Interaction
scope: An agent conducts a task through web documents, navigation and page actions while tracking page identity, asynchronous changes and action outcomes. The object is browser-specific task interaction through structured page observations or rendered interfaces.

title: Evidence-Driven Research Agent Orchestration
scope: An agent organizes an inquiry by tracking unresolved questions, selecting evidence-gathering actions, comparing findings and deciding when to synthesize or investigate further. Evidence sufficiency and provenance guide the action loop rather than merely decorating a generated answer.

excludes: A particular research assignment or report

title: Multi-Agent Role and Organization Design
scope: The allocation of task responsibilities, authority and interaction topology across agents. Roles and organization are considered together as the structure that determines who performs, supervises or integrates work.

title: Inter-Agent Communication Protocols
scope: The message contracts and exchange patterns by which agents communicate requests, evidence, commitments and results. It covers message interpretation and protocol state, including missing, duplicated or incompatible messages.

title: Multi-Agent Task Coordination
scope: The allocation and synchronization of interdependent agent work through commitments, scheduling and conflict resolution. The central object is how separately acting agents align progress toward a joint task under dependency constraints.

title: Multi-Agent Debate
scope: A protocol stages competing agent positions and responses before an adjudication step. It focuses on how contention, evidence and adjudication are organized, without assuming debate produces truth or independent evidence.

excludes: Independent peer review of a submitted artifact

title: Agent Peer Review
scope: A protocol assigns an agent to assess another agent's output against stated criteria and return actionable findings for revision or acceptance. It distinguishes independent checking from repetition of the producer's unsupported conclusions.

title: Shared State in Multi-Agent Coordination
scope: The coordination contract for agent access to shared task facts, ownership and updates, including visibility, conflicting writes and reconciled views. The object is the connection between shared information and agents' joint commitments.

title: Multi-Agent Failure Analysis
scope: A method for tracing a joint task failure through agent interactions, distinguishing local errors from coordination-induced propagation, circular dependencies and correlated unsupported agreement. Concrete failures serve as cases for diagnosis rather than being registered as Concept instances.

title: Evaluation of Multi-Agent Contributions and Coordination
scope: Evaluation designs distinguish joint-task outcomes from agent contributions and communication or coordination effects under comparable resource budgets. It addresses the attribution and interaction structure specific to multi-agent systems.

excludes: Generic confidence intervals and ablation methodology
Uncontrolled agent-count comparisons as evidence of benefit

title: Accelerator Execution of Tensor Workloads
scope: Map AI tensor contractions and attention workloads onto an available accelerator using tiling, data reuse and operation-shape choices. Analyze arithmetic work and memory traffic for a fixed model operator, including exact attention execution schedules that preserve its interaction rule.

excludes: Sparse or factorized changes to attention interactions in transformer.efficient_attention

title: AI Execution Runtimes
scope: The runtime representation, transformation and scheduling of AI computation graphs and tensor operations. It connects operator dispatch, memory lifetime and execution dependencies to a runnable model computation.

excludes: Automatic differentiation as a mathematical operation

title: Distributed Model Training
scope: The partitioning and synchronization of a model-training computation across workers using data, tensor, pipeline or related parallel decompositions. The object is preserving the intended training computation while coordinating parameter, gradient and activation communication.

title: Mixed-Precision Model Training
scope: The execution of a training computation with different numerical precisions for selected operations and stored quantities. It covers precision allocation and scaling or accumulation choices needed to maintain a usable training update under resource constraints.

title: Activation Checkpointing and Recomputation
scope: A training execution method stores selected intermediate activations and recomputes others when needed for gradient calculation. It owns the dependency-aware choice of retained values and the associated memory-computation schedule.

title: Model Serving and Request Scheduling
scope: The execution of model inference as a service with request admission, batching and scheduling across available compute. It explains the interaction between request arrival, prefill/decode work and service latency or throughput.

title: KV-Cache Memory Management
scope: The allocation, layout, sharing and reclamation of key/value cache storage across inference requests. The central problem is managing variable-length cached sequences within serving memory constraints.

excludes: Transformer cache computation mechanism in transformer.kv_cache

title: Neural Model Quantization
scope: Model deployment with reduced-precision representations for weights or activations, including scale selection and the mapping between stored values and computation. It owns representation choices and the resulting accuracy-resource assessment.

excludes: Mixed-precision training as a training schedule

title: Neural Model Pruning
scope: The removal of model weights, channels or other structure to produce a smaller or sparser executable model. It distinguishes structural removal from realized savings on the target execution system.

title: Speculative Decoding
scope: A decoding scheme proposes multiple candidate tokens using a cheaper draft process and checks them with a target model before committing output. It treats verification and acceptance rules as part of the mechanism and distinguishes distribution-preserving rules from approximate variants.

excludes: A blanket claim that every draft/verify variant preserves the target distribution

title: AI System Performance and Cost Modeling
scope: The construction of workload-level latency, throughput, memory and resource-cost models for AI execution. The object is locating bottlenecks and comparing feasible systems configurations under explicitly stated workload and accounting assumptions.

title: Agent Harness Architecture
scope: The architecture of the execution layer that mediates an agent's access to context, tools, task control, verification and persistent records. It defines component responsibilities and their interfaces around an agent decision loop.

excludes: A chapter collecting all harness mechanisms

title: Agent–Computer Interfaces and Execution Environments
scope: The execution interface that exposes computer capabilities and observations to an agent while translating accepted requests into controlled environment operations. Interface affordances and environment semantics are integrated through their effect on observable, executable actions.

excludes: Tool selection policy and tool-use training
Security threat models and sandbox mechanisms

title: Harness Context Lifecycle Integration
scope: The runtime integration that obtains context sources, invokes selection or compaction policies, and exposes a consistent context view at agent invocation boundaries. The object is the lifecycle contract between context construction and execution events.

includes: Context refresh triggers and source-to-invocation traceability
excludes: Persistent execution state as the source of truth

title: Agent Task Execution Control
scope: Runtime policies govern task admission, progress transitions, budgets, cancellation and termination around an agent loop. The object is enforcing which task transitions and further actions are permitted under an execution contract.

excludes: Human autonomy preferences and interface negotiation

title: Harness Verification Gates
scope: An execution pattern requires relevant external checks before accepting task progress or completion and routes failed or inconclusive checks back into the control loop. It distinguishes a model's completion assertion from evidence satisfying a specified acceptance condition.

excludes: Formal proof that an arbitrary task is correct

title: Harness Execution-State Integration
scope: The runtime contract that records accepted task transitions and synchronizes tool outcomes with persistent execution records used on subsequent invocations or resumes. It connects state-continuity mechanisms to the harness's live control flow.

includes: Ordering state updates relative to accepted execution events
excludes: Canonical-state and checkpoint mechanisms in LONG-STATE

title: Runtime Constraint Enforcement in Agent Harnesses
scope: A method translates declared execution constraints into checks at action or task-transition boundaries and specifies handling when a check fails. It distinguishes the constraint being enforced, the enforcement mechanism and the evidence available to the check.

excludes: Security sandbox and permission mechanisms as such
A universal correctness or safety guarantee

title: Harness Observability and Failure Diagnosis
scope: An instrumentation and diagnosis pattern relates task transitions, model invocations, tool effects and check outcomes in an execution trace. The central question is how an observed failure can be localized using evidence captured at harness boundaries.

title: Human Escalation in Agent Execution
scope: A runtime handoff protocol pauses or limits execution when a declared trigger requires human judgment, packages the relevant evidence and resumes from the human disposition. It owns the execution-state contract of escalation.

excludes: Human oversight interface design in humanai.oversight
Automatic authorization merely from elapsed time

title: Specification-Driven Agent Code Changes
scope: A workflow links a requested software change to explicit acceptance conditions, constrained agent edits and evidence that the implemented diff meets the intended change. The integration centers on maintaining correspondence between a specification and an agent-produced patch.

title: Repository Context for Coding Agents
scope: The construction of a coding agent's working view from repository structure, interfaces, dependencies and project instructions, with attention to authority and the current revision. The object is the mapping from a proposed code change to the repository evidence required to constrain it.

title: Agent Plan-to-Patch Execution
